scope: header_ecc.py now read whole across v29-v31:1-44,45-216,217-510,511-630,631-end. Syntax parsed; full module integrations and ECC backends not run.

findings.detail: Caller initializes corrupted false and iterates entry_asm without expected block-count/covered-byte assertion. Empty assembly from v29 skips all checks and leaves file uncounted as corrupt. Final success permits files_corrupted zero. Source-level caller chain; no full-backend reproduction yet.

Output reconstruction writes only assembled header blocks then seeks original to configured header_size. If short ECC omitted some header blocks but another block triggers reconstruction, missing header bytes are not copied before tail. This can shorten output; source-level consequence requiring end-to-end qualification.
Missing files, corrupted NUL paths and size mismatches increment skipped but do not force failure. Header mode shares all-skipped-success semantics with adaptive mode.
Tail is copied verbatim without integrity check; files_repaired_completely means classified header blocks, not verified complete original file. Post-repair accepts hash_ok OR ecc_ok.
Output wb is opened before original is reopened for tail copy. No path/physical-identity alias exclusion visible; overlap requires separate qualification, not an experiment on user files.
Generation and index are nontransactional; correction error list uses binary csv reader and basename-only path, with Latin-1 stored file paths. These repeat reviewed adaptive limitations.
